text:
ashley: Hi team — we have a customer (acct: acme-retail) reporting intermittent 500s and huge tail latency on /v1/embeddings. Started ~0900 UTC. They say requests usually 5–20ms but occasionally 800–1200ms. Suspect dynbatch behavior after recent routing change.

support-bot: [alert] embeddings-route-high-tail-latency acct=acme-retail p95=950ms p99=1100ms triggered at 1749994315

mikhail: thanks, can you paste the example request sizes and whether they use single or batched requests? also any auth errors in same timeframe?

ashley: customer uses mostly small single-doc embeds (text len ~120 tokens) at high qps (~800 rps) but they have periodic large batch jobs (N=1024 docs) every ~5m. No auth failures. Here's truncated logs around one spike:

```
[09:12:11.342] coalescer: incoming=820 window_ms=50 max_batch=64 formed_batches=13 avg_batch=62
[09:12:11.343] runtime: dispatch latency=6ms
[09:12:11.343] coalescer: burst_in=1024 high_var=true
[09:12:11.343] batcher: overflow=true dropped=0 queued=980
[09:12:11.344] coalescer: drop_window_skip=3
[09:12:12.155] runtime: tail_latency=1180ms
```

elaine: that logs smells like the coalescer/window skipped because large burst came in that overran queue. drop_window_skip=3 indicates some batches skipped the flush window to make room. Max_batch was 64 but you see formed_batches=13 which implies many concurrent batches queued.

mikhail: what's the customer's config for dynamic batching (max_batch_size, coalesce_window_ms, queue_capacity)?

ashley: their service config (from their dedicated env) — pasted (sanitized):

```
embeddings:
  dynamic_batching: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  coalesce_window_ms: 50
  queue_capacity: 1024
  priority_preempt: false
```

ops-oncall: two quick thoughts: (1) queue_capacity large + coalesce_window_ms big makes room for a lot of small reqs to pile up, then periodic giant job causes queue thrash. (2) priority_preempt=false means the batcher can't preempt/slot big jobs so they cause head-of-line blocking for subsequent small requests, producing tail spikes.

elaine: agree. Also noticed "drop_window_skip" logged — that's our batcher skipping a flush window because next big batch didn't fit into the current slot. I want to see the batcher metrics around coalesce_waiters and slot_utilization for that period. ashley, can you pull metrics: batcher.coalesce_waiters, batcher.window_skips, batcher.queue_depth, runtime.active_workers between 09:10–09:15?

ashley: grabbing now, brb. (copied links to metrics screenshot)

ashley: metrics: coalesce_waiters peaked 980, window_skips=4 spikes at same time, queue_depth ~1000, active_workers=16 (concurrency 16 per shard). Customer is on dedicated shard config with 16 workers.

mikhail: this is classic starvation + waterfalling. The large job floods queue; batcher forms many full batches back-to-back, pushing small single-doc requests into late windows. Because coalesce_window_ms is 50ms and concurrency limited to 16, small requests wait multiple windows -> tail latency skyrockets.

ops-oncall: short remediation steps to suggest to customer (low-friction):
- set priority_preempt=true if available (enables small-high-priority requests to cut into batches)
- decrease coalesce_window_ms to 8–12ms for their latency-sensitive pipeline
- increase max_batch_size to 128 OR add a separate route for large bulk jobs (recommended)

elaine: also recommend enabling "batching.stats_export=true" and setting queue_capacity to 512 to reduce waterfall amplitude.

ashley: I've suggested the above and customer asked for repro steps so they can validate. Can you provide a small script they can run to reproduce the tail spike locally against staging (non-prod) embeddings endpoint?

mikhail: here's a simple repro plan — two concurrent generators:
1) flooder: steady small single-item requests at 800 rps (size ~120 tokens)
2) bulk: every 5m send a single large batch of 1024 small docs

Curl-ish example (python pseudocode):

```
# flooder thread
while True:
  requests.post('/v1/embeddings', json={'input': 'a'*600})
  sleep(0.00125)  # ~800 rps

# bulk thread (every 300s)
while True:
  payload = {'input': ['doc']*1024}
  requests.post('/v1/embeddings', json=payload)
  sleep(300)
```

This should reproduce coalesce_queue blowup and window_skips.

ashley: thanks — shared repro and config changes. Customer tried priority_preempt=true and coalesce_window_ms=12ms; initial results look promising — p99 dropped from ~1100ms to ~45ms. They want us to patch default behavior to avoid other customers hitting this. Any objections to recommending defaults: coalesce_window_ms=12, max_batch_size=128, priority_preempt=true for dedicated pools? Want SRE signoff.

ops-oncall: sounds reasonable as a tuned default for low-latency tenants. A couple cautions: increasing max_batch_size has CPU/memory implications for model kernels — need perf QA for heavy models. Also enabling preemption changes ordering semantics; must document.

mikhail: agree with ops. Suggest rollout plan:
- stage change in canary tenants for 48h (monitor p50/p95/p99, throughput)
- add an alert for queue_depth > 600 and window_skips > 2
- update docs and add a section in console recommendations for mixed workloads

elaine: I'll file a follow-up internal ticket (ENG-12258) to track default change + QA. ashley, add the customer case ref (SUP-5719) and close when they confirm stable.

ashley: will do. Customer confirmed staging results and will let us know after 24h. marking as escalated -> ENG-12258, cc ops-oncall. :thumbsup:

support-bot: [escalation created] ENG-12258 linked -> SUP-5719

ashley: thanks everyone. keeping thread open until after 24h validation.
